name: GM Gen III (1997–2007 LS-era V8, 4.3/5.3/6.0 truck engines)

pcms.pcmhammer: experimental — check current release notes before relying on it

binFormat.segmentTable: 0x514 — seven {start,end} uint32 BE pairs (EngineCal, EngineDiag, TransCal, TransDiag, Fuel, System, Speedo)
binFormat.checksums: 16-bit two's-complement big-endian word sums, stored at each segment start (OS at 0x500)

adapters.device: A VPW-capable J2534 interface you have proven
adapters.notes: The only rule that matters for writes. Must genuinely implement J1850 VPW; 4x support turns a 30-minute read into a few minutes. Prove it on something you can afford to lose before trusting it with a write.
Native to its own software; many also work as a general J2534 pass-thru.
Purpose-built interfaces with 4x support are the community's usual recommendation for PCMHammer — see pcmhammer.github.io/users/supported-devices.
Often work at 1x only: a 512 KB full read takes 30+ minutes, so a battery maintainer is mandatory.

adapters.device: Interfaces that claim VPW without implementing it
adapters.notes: Several exist, and some cheap clones omit the J1850 circuitry entirely. Check community reports for your exact model before buying.
